title: Reporting on Brain Health & Research: A Poynter Fellowship (2026-2027)
description: A year-long, fully funded fellowship for journalists to deepen or expand their reporting on brain health, brain science, and related research, run by the Poynter Institute (a nonprofit journalism school and research organization) with funding from the Brain and Behavior Research Foundation. Thirty journalists are selected from across the United States, spanning all platforms, beats, and experience levels -- including health, science, and public affairs reporters as well as journalists new to the brain-health beat. The fellowship begins with a three-day in-person opening convening at Poynter's campus in St. Petersburg, Florida in December 2026, followed by monthly virtual workshops and individualized coaching throughout 2027. Travel and lodging for the in-person convening are fully covered, and fellows who complete the program (attending all convenings/workshops, producing quarterly reporting, and completing a fellowship project) receive a $3,000 stipend. This appears to be the inaugural cohort of this specific fellowship. Because the primary application page sits behind a network restriction that blocked direct verification during this research pass, these details were cross-referenced across Poynter's own press release, the CASW Connector science-writers' event calendar, and independent trade-press coverage (newsroomamerica.com), all of which converge on the same deadline, stipend, and 'fully funded' terms.
visaNote: This is a part-time journalism fellowship, not employment; it is intended for journalists already based in the United States.
